subject: Order Form — entity swap, invoicing path & tax holdback
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@medicore.com>, procurement@medicore.com
Date: 2027-05-25T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form draft — entity / invoicing questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the draft. We reviewed with procurement and legal and have three items that need clarity before we can sign:

1) Entity for invoicing — our accounting prefers invoices to be issued to MediCore, Inc. (US) rather than our EU subsidiary. Is Redwood able to route invoicing to the US entity while the Services are technically procured by MediCore EU?

2) Tax holdback — for EU spend, our tax team requires a clause outlining who bears withholding/VAT risk if local authorities treat the payment differently. Can you confirm Redwood's position (especially on VAT reverse-charge vs withholding obligations)?

3) Min-commit phasing — we may want to stage the 12-month minimum commit across two legal entities later in the term. Do you accept an entity substitution flow with evidence and advance notice?

I've attached our redline (Medico_OrderForm_redline_20270525.pdf) and a short procurement checklist.

Can you please confirm whether Redwood can: (a) invoice into the US entity, (b) accept an entity substitution process, and (c) provide the tax evidence your finance team needs?

Best,
Lena
Senior Procurement Manager
MediCore

Attachment: Medico_OrderForm_redline_20270525.pdf (redline PDF, 4 pages)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form draft — entity / invoicing questions

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Quick answers up front and we can follow with formal language:

(a) Invoicing to US entity: Yes, we can invoice MediCore, Inc. (US) provided: (i) the US PO references the Redwood order form/deal id, and (ii) the US entity accepts tax and indemnity allocation as noted below. We'll need your PO and the remit details.

(b) Entity substitution: We support a controlled entity substitution process (not automatic). Our ask is: 30 days' notice, written confirmation of equivalence (same commercial terms), and KYC/tax evidence for the incoming entity. We'll draft a short exhibit for the order form that captures the flow.

(c) Tax evidence: Redwood can provide invoice-level detail and historical consumption reports. For legal evidence (e.g., certificates of tax residency), we'll need MediCore to provide your forms; we've attached a Tax_Evidence_Template.xlsx that outlines standard items we typically rely on.

Looping in Kimberly (sales ops) for PO/invoice routing and Karthik (legal) for suggested clause text. We'll confirm language and send an amended order form tomorrow.

Next steps:
- Kimberly: confirm invoicing routing and whether our billing team needs any additional fields on the PO.
- Karthik: can you draft the substitution exhibit + short tax holdback paragraph for review?

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Tax_Evidence_Template.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form draft — entity / invoicing questions

Hi all — quick ops note on invoicing routing and PO requirements so Finance can process without delays: 

- Invoices: Our billing system accepts remit-to: MediCore, Inc. (US) with the following mandatory PO fields: PO number, bill-to entity, remit address, and tax ID. Without the PO we can't change the invoice recipient post-issuance.
- Currency: If invoicing to the US entity, currency must be USD to avoid cross-entity FX complications. If MediCore wants EUR invoices to EU entity, we can do that too but that's a different remit path.
- Minimum commit phasing: we can accept phased invoicing (e.g., 6 months upfront + 6 months invoice later) but pricing bands tied to a minimum commitment must be reconciled at month 6 for true-up. For accounting, we prefer invoicing aligned with entity that holds the spend for tax purposes.

Operational asks for MediCore to expedite sign: please share the US PO and remit details, and confirm the currency. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call with Billing and Tax to close the last mile.

Kimberly Park
Revenue Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form draft — entity / invoicing questions

Hi Lena — thanks for the redline and the questions. Below are proposed guardrails and a succinct clause we can include in the Order Form (or an exhibit) to handle entity substitution and tax holdback. Happy to iterate.

1) Entity substitution (proposed):
- Redwood agrees to accept an invoicing entity substitution where (i) MediCore provides 30 days' advance written notice, (ii) MediCore supplies tax residency certificates and evidence of equivalent commercial terms, and (iii) the parties execute a simple Assignment & Billing Exhibit confirming the substitution.

2) Tax holdback / withholding (proposed paragraph):
- "Tax Withholding; VAT. If any governmental authority imposes a withholding tax, VAT, or other tax on payments due under this Order Form, the party required to withhold shall (i) notify the other party promptly, (ii) use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize the tax, and (iii) provide documentary evidence of payment or withholding. Redwood will remit gross amounts unless applicable law requires tax withholding, in which case MediCore agrees to provide evidence to support tax relief (e.g., certificate of residence). Any increase in net cost attributable to a withholding obligation applicable solely to MediCore's chosen invoicing route shall be borne by MediCore unless otherwise agreed in writing."
3) Practical evidence: the Tax_Evidence_Template.xlsx Naomi attached is a good start — we need certificates of residence, local VAT registration, and a statement on whether reverse-charge applies. For EU reverse-charge, typically MediCore must confirm that the reverse-charge applies on a per-invoice basis.

4) Net terms: Redwood standard is Net 45 for enterprise; we can offer Net 30 for US-based government or large enterprise with credit review. For this deal, Net 45 stands unless Procurement requests credit terms and provides PO/bank references.

I'll push a clean Order Form with an exhibit capturing (1) substitution flow and (2) the tax paragraph for your review by EOD. If MediCore prefers, we can also capture a short fallback that ties invoicing currency to the invoiced entity.

—Karthik
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medicore.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Final: next steps on order form & DocuSign

Hi Lena — quick follow-up after internal alignment.

Summary / next steps:
1) We've incorporated Karthik's language and an "Assignment & Billing Exhibit" draft into the Order Form to handle entity substitution + tax holdback.
2) Billing confirmed they can invoice MediCore, Inc. (US) in USD once we receive a PO with the mandatory fields Kimberly listed.
3) Net terms: Redwood will remain Net 45 for this contract. If MediCore provides credit references and requests Net 30, we can evaluate but need Finance sign-off.
4) Tax evidence: please upload certificates of residence and VAT registration to the Drive folder linked below; the Tax_Evidence_Template.xlsx shows the exact files we need.

We've prepared a DocuSign packet with the updated Order Form and a short exhibit. Signing flow we propose: (a) MediCore signs the Order Form (US entity as invoice recipient), (b) MediCore provides PO to billing@redwood.com, (c) MediCore uploads tax evidence to the Drive folder.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC-DocuSign-123
Drive (upload tax evidence): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-orderform-evidence

If that aligns, I'll send the DocuSign invite now. If we should keep invoicing to EU entity instead, let us know ASAP and we'll swap the remit path (EUR invoices / EU remit).

Thanks and looking forward to getting this across the line — Naomi
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: DocuSign packet (Order Form + Assignment & Billing Exhibit)
